clue.text: See 2
Stewed lamb's tail brought up

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, so only the end of lamb's is taken

parts.note: lamb, read without its possessive; its tail is B
to bring up a child is to raise it, so brought up means raised

explanation.surface: A recipe note: the lamb's tail was stewed and then served.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is slow cooking in a little liquid in a covered pot, which is a kind of stewing.

clue.text: Clumsy — audience's sympathetic during a friend's dance

indicators.note: an audience hears rather than reads, so the phrase is what the letters sound like when spoken

parts.note: a sympathetic character is likeable; during means in; the indefinite article, A; china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a friend's is a china's; a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Someone clumsy is being forgiven by onlookers because they were dancing with a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, LIKEABLE IN A CHINA'S HOP becomes the idiom. China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so a china is a friend; a hop is an old word for a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone blundering carelessly about, like a bovine let loose among fragile crockery.

clue.text: Cold storage facilities having no news once sunshine's blazing

indicators.note: blazing suggests things are wild and out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order
having no says some letters of the mix are thrown away before rearranging

parts.note: sunshine, the possessive just linking it to blazing
read as N's, plural of N for new: here all three Ns in the fodder

explanation.surface: The cold stores have no news to report while the sun blazes outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove every N (news read as N's) from ONCE SUNSHINE'S, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Icehouses were buildings, often partly underground, where ice was stored through the year before refrigerators.

clue.text: Posh interrupting a group of footballers before international — tip for team is familiar

indicators.note: before says these pieces come ahead of what follows
interrupting means breaking into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football
U means upper class or posh, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, so only the start of team is used

parts.note: first letter of team

explanation.surface: A posh player breaks into a football side before an international, with a tip for the team.
explanation.walkthrough: Put U inside A FA to make AUFA, then add I and the first letter of team.
explanation.definitionFit: Au fait is French borrowed into English for being well acquainted with or knowledgeable about something.

clue.text: Dodgy cult claims universal knowledge

indicators.note: claims is taken as holds or takes in, so cult wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a cult is a sect
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
SP, short for starting price in horse racing, is slang for inside information or knowledge

explanation.surface: A shady cult says it knows everything.
explanation.walkthrough: SP is the starting price in betting, which came to mean the inside information in general, as in 'what's the SP?'
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgy and suspect are both informal ways of saying something is doubtful or untrustworthy.

clue.text: Feel slur affected political autonomy

indicators.note: affected means altered or changed, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician feels hurt by a slur during a debate about independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-rule is government of a country by its own people, which is what political autonomy means.

clue.text: Truss extremely upset — to begin with only one conservative resigned

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read from bottom to top
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of Truss

indicators.note: to begin with points to the very start of the next word

parts.note: first letter of only
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Liz Truss, the Conservative prime minister, upset and alone, resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: Liz Truss resigned as UK prime minister in October 2022, weeks before this puzzle appeared, so 'resigned' looks like news; it is the definition, meaning uncomplaining.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic accepts hardship without complaint, so stoic and resigned share the sense of patient acceptance.

clue.text: Per diems fiddled — I invested in waterproof layer?

indicators.note: invested in means put into, so one letter goes inside the others
fiddled means falsified or tampered with, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to padding their daily expenses claims and putting money into a waterproofing business.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the skin is only loosely a waterproof layer.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin, which keeps water from passing in or out of the body.

clue.text: Tying up guards for starters, then woman regularly breaks into BT Tower

indicators.note: then says this piece follows the previous one
starters are the opening parts, so the first letter of each of these words is taken

parts.note: first letter of Tying
first letter of up
first letter of guards

indicators.note: breaks into means gets inside, so these letters go within the other piece
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the even letters of woman give O and A

explanation.surface: A security story: guards are tied up while a woman breaks into London's BT Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' reads as the BT Tower in London, but it is the definition: something that tows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tugboat pulls ships into harbour, so it is literally something that tows, the crossword-style reading of tower.

clue.text: Cross husband leaves finally — roll the joint

indicators.note: leaves means goes away, so this letter is removed

parts.note: an ankh is the Egyptian looped cross

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of each of the following words

parts.note: last letter of roll
last letter of the

explanation.surface: An angry husband walks out, and someone decides to roll a cannabis joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the Egyptian ankh; 'joint' looks like cannabis, but it is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge where the foot meets the leg, one of the body's joints.

clue.text: Silliness curtailed by outstanding fans

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: folly is silliness
an outstanding debt is one still owing

explanation.surface: Fans are cutting down on their silly behaviour for a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as excellent, but here it means unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a body of supporters or admirers, so it is a collective word for fans.

clue.text: West's involvement in Rhodesia's dissolution appears to be less substantial

indicators.note: involvement in means being drawn inside, so this letter goes within the other letters
dissolution means breaking up, so the letters of the country's name are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of Rhodesia, ignoring the possessive
W is the abbreviation for west

explanation.surface: A historian downplays the West's role in Rhodesia breaking up.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhodesia was the former name of Zimbabwe. Rearrange RHODESIA to SHADOIER and put W inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shadowy is vague and insubstantial, so shadowier is the comparative, meaning flimsier or harder to pin down.

clue.text: Wine business takes belief

indicators.note: takes means holds within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
red is a wine

explanation.surface: A wine company adopts a creed for its brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith, from the Latin 'I believe' that opens the Creed.

clue.text: Partly decorates a bedroom in retirement to add value? Far from it!

definitions.text: to add value? Far from it!

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run backwards
partly means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone decorates a bedroom when they retire to increase the house's value, but it does the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an ironic one: adding value is the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To debase is to lower the worth or quality of something, the reverse of adding value.

clue.text: Problem arising with contrived sequel — it's supposed to be entertaining

indicators.note: in a down clue, arising means going upwards, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rub is a problem, as in 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: contrived means artificially put together, so the letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A film critic complains that a forced sequel is meant to amuse but does not.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a comic, often bawdy, variety show or parody intended to amuse an audience.

clue.text: Student wearing dull top backwards — it offers thermal protection

indicators.note: backwards means the whole piece is read from end to start

parts.note: tame means dull or unexciting

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the letter sits inside the other piece

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle
L is for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A student wears a dull top backwards to keep warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backwards' sounds like the way the top is worn, but it reverses everything that comes before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A place mat goes under a plate on the table to protect the surface from heat.

clue.text: See 2
Hunt and Truss mostly broadcast lies

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are reworked
mostly means most but not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Jeremy Hunt and Liz Truss, Conservative politicians, are said to have put out lies on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Hunt replaced Truss's chancellor in October 2022. Drop the last S of Truss to get TRUS, then mix with HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untruths are false statements, which is what lies are.

clue.text: Cheap excuse to drop tab amidst confusion

indicators.note: amidst means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: fog is a state of confusion

indicators.note: to drop means to let fall, so this letter is removed

parts.note: a reason can be an excuse
E is slang for ecstasy, which comes as a tablet or tab

explanation.surface: Someone in a muddle makes a cheap excuse for taking an ecstasy pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' is drug slang for swallowing a pill, and E for ecstasy is the tab; here dropping it means taking it away.
explanation.definitionFit: Bought for a song is an idiom for very cheaply, for next to nothing.

clue.text: Appropriate to protect local sculpture, say

indicators.note: to protect means to surround and shelter, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: fit means appropriate or suitable
local means near at hand

explanation.surface: A council thinks it right to protect a local sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpture is an example of fine art, the visual arts made for beauty rather than use; 'say' flags the example.

clue.text: Maternal grandmother taking in Italy's foul atmosphere

indicators.note: taking in means holding within, so one letter goes inside

parts.note: a mother's mother is ma's ma
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Grandma takes in the stale air of Italy on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unpleasant or unhealthy vapour, once thought to carry disease.

clue.text: Sinatra's working, making number exciting, principally for dancer

indicators.note: working means being worked on or kneaded, so the letters are rearranged
making ... for joins with for to say one letter stands in place of another
for means in place of, so one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: the letters of Sinatra, ignoring the possessive

indicators.note: principally means chiefly or first, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: first letter of exciting

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra is at work, making a song-and-dance number exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the N in SINATRA to E, giving SIEATRA, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was the American film star famous for his tap and ballroom dancing.

clue.text: Confused — put on light

parts.note: to add is to put on top of something
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a small light

explanation.surface: Someone is muddled and switches on a light.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or unable to think clearly, so it is a synonym of confused.

clue.text: Attempt to contact the dead — assuming that is not main relative

indicators.note: assuming means taking on or into oneself, so one piece goes inside the other
not means without, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: a seance is a meeting to try to reach the spirits of the dead
the main is the sea
IE is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A medium attempts a seance, assuming the departed is not a main relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family member, so she is a relative.

clue.text: Cream from Aldi, regularly described by French and English

indicators.note: described by means drawn around, so the outer piece encircles the inner

parts.note: et is French for and

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so alternate letters are taken

parts.note: the even letters of Aldi give L and I

explanation.surface: Cream bought from Aldi, the supermarket chain, is described in French and English on the label.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its best part, and the elite are the best of a group.

clue.text: Favourite racecourse's first to provide VIP treatment

indicators.note: first says this piece comes at the start, ahead of the other

parts.note: Redcar is a racecourse in North Yorkshire
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: The favourite at a racecourse wins and gets star treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favourite' looks like the racing favourite, but it is PET; Redcar, a seaside town in North Yorkshire, has a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling out the red carpet means giving a guest special ceremonial welcome.

clue.text: Cruise company theatre's opening for start of drag show

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter replaces another

parts.note: P&O is a British cruise and shipping company, read as P AND O

indicators.note: start of points to the first letter of drag

parts.note: first letter of drag

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of theatre's

explanation.surface: A cruise line opens a theatre on board to stage a drag show.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is spelt out as P AND O; change its D for T. Panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show, often with a man in drag as the dame.
explanation.definitionFit: A panto is a comic family stage show performed in Britain around Christmas.

clue.text: American court about to stop gangster getting discharge

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to quit is to stop
Al Capone was the famous Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: An American court is about to end the trial of a gangster by releasing him.
explanation.definitionFit: An acquittal sets a defendant free from a charge, which is a form of discharge in law.

clue.text: Deer essentially bit tongue

parts.note: a hind is a female deer

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence or core, so the middle letter is taken

parts.note: middle letter of bit

explanation.surface: A deer essentially bit someone's tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like the body part, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindi is a major language of India, and tongue is an old word for a language.

clue.text: Pegs go inside tents

indicators.note: inside means within, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: tees are the small pegs a golf ball sits on
go is a euphemism for urinate, pee

explanation.surface: Tent pegs are put in place inside the tents.
explanation.definitionFit: Teepees are conical tents traditionally used by Native American peoples of the Plains.

clue.text: Strongly disapprove of part changing hands after actor Johnny's quietly sacked

indicators.note: after says this piece follows the previous one
sacked means dismissed, so this letter is thrown out

parts.note: Johnny Depp is the American actor
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: changing hands means swapping the hand letters, left and right, within the word

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: People strongly object to actor Johnny Depp being quietly dropped from a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' means the left-hand and right-hand letters, L and R, trade places within the word for part.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something is to condemn it or regret it strongly.
